name_en: Tenshinhan — a crab omelette set over rice with a sweet-savory starch-thickened sauce
summary_ja: 卵でとじたかに玉を白飯にのせ、酸味と甘みのある醤油あんをかけた丼。中国には対応する料理がなく、日本で生まれたとされる。発祥は東京・浅草説と大阪説が並び立ち、決着していない。
summary_en: A crab omelette set over rice and finished with a sweet-tangy, starch-thickened soy sauce. No dish in China matches it, and it's said to have been born in Japan — though whether in Tokyo's Asakusa or in Osaka remains an open question.
source_title: 天津飯の起源―定説を疑う―
source_publisher: 日本国際情報学会『Kokusai-Joho』3巻1号

name_en: Hiyashi chuka — chilled ramen noodles topped with shredded egg, ham, and vegetables in a tangy sauce
summary_ja: 茹でた中華麺を冷水で締め、錦糸卵やハム、きゅうりを彩りよく並べて酢の効いたたれをかける夏の麺。中国の冷たい和え麺「涼拌麺」がヒントとされるが、酢醤油だれで食べる形は日本で独自に育ったという。
summary_en: Chinese-style noodles are chilled in water and topped in neat rows of shredded egg, ham, and cucumber, then finished with a tangy sauce — a summer dish said to take its cue from China's liangban mian but to have grown into its own soy-vinegar form in Japan.
source_title: 龍亭について（冷やし中華の由来）

name_en: Tanmen — stir-fried vegetables and pork in a clear salted broth over ramen noodles
summary_ja: 強火で炒めたもやしやキャベツ、豚肉を鶏がらの塩味スープに落とし、中華麺と合わせる麺料理。中国語の「湯麺」はスープ麺全般を指す言葉だが、日本のタンメンはこの名で独自の一皿として定着したとされる。
summary_en: Bean sprouts, cabbage, and pork stir-fried over high heat go into a clear, salted chicken broth with ramen noodles. Chinese 'tangmian' just means noodles in soup generally, but Japan's tanmen is said to have settled into its own specific dish under that name.

name_en: Nira-reba itame — stir-fried liver and garlic chives in a soy-oyster sauce glaze
summary_ja: 豚や牛のレバーをにんにくやしょうがで下味をつけ、にらともやしと強火で炒め合わせる定食の定番。中国の家庭料理がもとにあるとされ、日本では醤油とオイスターソースで濃いめに仕立てる。
summary_en: Pork or beef liver, marinated in garlic and ginger, is stir-fried fast with chives and bean sprouts — a set-meal staple said to trace to a Chinese home dish, given a stronger soy-and-oyster-sauce finish in Japan.
source_title: レバニラ？ニラレバ？正しいのはどっち！？

name_en: Chahan — Japanese-style fried rice with egg, scallion, and pork, tossed loose over high heat
summary_ja: 卵と刻んだねぎ、豚肉やハムを白飯と一緒に強火でぱらりと炒め合わせる、中華食堂の定番。広東の炒飯を手本にしながらも、日本では具や味付けが独自に整理され、半人前の「半チャーハン」という食べ方まで定着したという。
summary_en: Egg, chopped scallion, and pork or ham are stir-fried loose with rice over high heat — a diner staple said to take Cantonese fried rice as its model while settling, in Japan, into its own pared-down ingredients and even its own half-size 'han-chahan' order.

name_en: Subuta — Japanese sweet-and-sour pork, cubed and glazed in a ketchup-tinted starch sauce
summary_ja: 揚げた豚肉に、片栗粉でとろみをつけたケチャップ入りの甘酢あんを絡める中華食堂の定番。広東の古老肉が手本とされるが、パイナップルを入れるかどうかで意見が分かれる、日本ならではの論争を抱えている。
summary_en: Fried pork cubes are glazed in a cornstarch-thickened, ketchup-tinted sweet-and-sour sauce — a diner staple said to take Cantonese gulaorou as its model, while carrying a distinctly Japanese debate over whether pineapple belongs in it.

name_en: Ebi chiri — shrimp in a mild, ketchup-tinted chili sauce
summary_ja: 殻をむいたえびを、豆板醤の辛さにケチャップの甘みを重ねたとろみあんで仕上げる料理。四川の「乾焼蝦仁」を、四川出身の料理人が日本人向けに辛さを和らげて考案したと伝わる。
summary_en: Shelled shrimp are finished in a thickened sauce that layers ketchup's sweetness over doubanjiang's heat — said to have been created by a Sichuan-born chef who softened Sichuan's ganshao xiaren to suit Japanese palates.
source_title: 四川飯店発祥！？エビチリの美味さの秘密

name_en: Ebi mayo — fried shrimp tossed in a sweet mayonnaise sauce
summary_ja: 衣をつけて揚げたえびに、マヨネーズをベースにした甘いソースを絡める料理。広東料理の料理人が、アメリカで食べたマヨネーズがけのえび料理に納得がいかず、独自に作り直したのが始まりとされる。
summary_en: Battered, fried shrimp are tossed in a sweet mayonnaise-based sauce — said to have begun when a Cantonese chef, unsatisfied with a mayonnaise-dressed shrimp dish he'd eaten in the United States, remade it his own way.

name_en: Mabo dofu — Japanese-style mapo tofu, milder and often made with pork instead of beef
summary_ja: 豆腐と挽き肉を、豆板醤や甜麺醤で辛みと甘みをつけたとろみあんで煮込む料理。本場四川の花椒の痺れる辛さを控え、牛肉を豚肉に置き換えるなど、四川出身の料理人が日本人向けに作り替えたと伝わる。
summary_en: Tofu and ground meat are simmered in a thickened sauce built on doubanjiang and sweet bean paste — said to have been reworked for Japan by a Sichuan-born chef, who eased off Sichuan's numbing peppercorn heat and, later, swapped beef for pork.
source_title: 麻婆豆腐、回鍋肉、青椒肉絲…「四川料理の魂」

name_en: Mabo nasu — eggplant and ground pork simmered in the same sauce as mabo dofu
summary_ja: 揚げ焼きにした茄子と挽き肉を、麻婆豆腐と同じ豆板醤や甜麺醤の合わせだれで煮る料理。本場四川の「魚香茄子」とは調味の系統が異なり、日本の合わせ調味料の普及とともに広まったとされる。
summary_en: Pan-fried eggplant and ground pork are simmered in the same doubanjiang-and-sweet-bean-paste sauce as mabo dofu — a different family of seasoning from Sichuan's yuxiang qiezi, said to have spread with the rise of packaged Japanese seasoning mixes.

name_en: Hoikoro — Japanese-style twice-cooked pork stir-fried with cabbage in a sweet miso glaze
summary_ja: 豚肉とキャベツを甜麺醤ベースの甘辛いたれで炒め合わせる料理。本場四川ではにんにくの茎などの葉野菜を使うが、日本では手に入りやすいキャベツに置き換わり、独自の型として広まったとされる。
summary_en: Pork and cabbage are stir-fried in a sweet, miso-like glaze — said to have swapped Sichuan's leafy garlic stems for cabbage, easier to source in Japan, and settled into its own form from there.
source_title: 回鍋肉とは？四川伝統料理の魅力を解説

name_en: Chinjao roosu — shredded beef and green pepper stir-fried in oyster sauce
summary_ja: 細切りにした肉とピーマンを油通ししてから炒め合わせる料理。本場中国では豚肉が基本とされるが、日本では牛肉を使う店が多く、オイスターソースで仕上げる型が定着しているという。
summary_en: Shredded meat and green pepper, passed through hot oil, are stir-fried together — a dish said to use pork as its base in China, while beef and an oyster-sauce finish became the common choice in Japan.

name_en: Kanitama — a fluffy whole-egg omelette folded around crab meat
summary_ja: ほぐした蟹の身を溶き卵と合わせ、ふんわりと焼き上げる料理。中国の「芙蓉蟹」は卵白だけを使う白い仕上げだが、日本のかに玉は全卵を使うため黄色く、この違いが天津飯を生む土台になったとされる。
summary_en: Shredded crab meat is folded into beaten egg and cooked soft — China's furong xie uses only egg whites and comes out white, while Japan's whole-egg version turns yellow, a gap said to have set the stage for tenshinhan.
source_title: 天津飯の起源―定説を疑う―
source_publisher: 日本国際情報学会『Kokusai-Joho』3巻1号

name_en: Harumaki — thin-wrappered Japanese spring rolls fried until crisp
summary_ja: 豚肉やたけのこ、しいたけなどの具を薄い皮で巻き、油でかりっと揚げる点心。広東の春巻きが手本とされるが、日本では皮を薄く仕立てて具の水分を抑え、独自の食感に整えられているという。
summary_en: Pork, bamboo shoot, and shiitake are rolled in a thin wrapper and fried crisp — a dim sum item said to take Cantonese spring rolls as its model, refined in Japan into its own light, crisp texture with a thinner skin.

name_en: Nikudango — deep-fried ground pork meatballs glazed in a sweet-and-sour sauce
summary_ja: 丸めた挽き肉を揚げ、酢豚と同じ甘酢あんをからめる料理。中国の獅子頭のような大ぶりの蒸し団子とは違い、日本では一口大に揚げてケチャップ系のあんで仕上げる、弁当や給食向けの型が広まったとされる。
summary_en: Ground pork is rolled into balls, fried, and glazed in the same sweet-and-sour sauce as subuta — smaller and fried, unlike China's large steamed 'lion's head' meatballs, and said to have spread as a bento and school-lunch staple.

name_en: Tantanmen — a Japanese sesame-and-chili noodle soup, adapted from a dry Sichuan noodle snack
summary_ja: ごまだれと辣油を効かせた挽き肉入りのスープに中華麺を合わせる料理。本場四川の担担面は汁のない和え麺だが、日本では大ぶりの丼にたっぷりのスープを張る、汁あり仕立てに作り替えられたとされる。
summary_en: Ramen noodles go into a chili-and-sesame soup topped with minced pork — Sichuan's original dandan noodles are a small, brothless dish, tossed rather than served in soup, but Japan's version is said to have been rebuilt as a full bowl of soup noodles.

name_en: Taiwan mazesoba — brothless noodles tossed with spicy minced pork, garlic, and a raw egg yolk
summary_ja: 台湾ラーメンの具「台湾ミンチ」を、スープではなく茹でた麺に直接からめて食べる汁なし麺。2008年に名古屋の一軒の店が、失敗作を廃棄する寸前にひらめいたことから生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: Taiwan mince, the topping from Taiwan ramen, is tossed straight onto boiled noodles with no broth at all — said to have been born in 2008 at a single Nagoya shop, moments before a failed batch was about to be thrown out.

name_en: Chuka soba — the old Tokyo name for a clear soy-sauce ramen, from the earliest Chinese-noodle diners
summary_ja: 醤油だれに鶏や豚のだしを合わせたすっきりとしたスープに、細めの中華麺を合わせる型。1910年に浅草で創業した中国料理店が、東京の醤油ラーメンの草分けとされ、その屋号を継ぐように「中華そば」の名が今も使われているという。
summary_en: Thin Chinese-style noodles sit in a clean soy-sauce broth built on chicken and pork stock — a style traced to a Chinese restaurant that opened in Asakusa in 1910, said to be the pioneer of Tokyo's soy-sauce ramen, its old name 'chuka soba' still used by some shops today.

name_en: Kanton men — ramen noodles topped with a thick, mixed-vegetable and meat gravy
summary_ja: 炒めた豚肉や野菜をとろみのある餡に仕立て、ラーメンの麺の上にかける料理。名前に「広東」を冠しながら、実際の広東料理には対応する料理がなく、日本で生まれた中華料理の一つとされる。
summary_en: Stir-fried pork and vegetables are worked into a thick gravy and poured over ramen noodles — a dish that carries the name 'Canton' despite having no counterpart in actual Cantonese cooking, said to be one of Japan's own inventions.

name_ja: 五目あんかけ焼きそば
name_en: Gomoku ankake yakisoba — noodles fried crisp and topped with a thick mixed-vegetable gravy
summary_ja: 揚げ焼きにしてかりっと仕上げた中華麺に、豚肉や野菜、海鮮を炒めたとろみあんをかける料理。広東麺と同じ餡を使いながら、麺を汁なしで香ばしく揚げる点で分かれた、日本の中華食堂発の一皿とされる。
summary_en: Chinese noodles are pan-fried crisp, then topped with a thick gravy of stir-fried pork, vegetables, and seafood — a dish said to share its gravy with kanton men while branching off by frying the noodles dry and crisp, a Japanese diner invention.

name_en: Chashu — soy-braised pork, the simmered style that became standard in Japanese ramen
summary_ja: 豚のばら肉やもも肉を醤油だれでじっくり煮込んだ具材。中国の叉焼はたれを塗って炙り焼きにするのが本来の型とされるが、日本のラーメン店では煮て作る「煮豚」の型が広く定着しているという。
summary_en: Pork belly or leg is simmered slowly in a soy-based sauce — where China's char siu is traditionally roasted with a glaze, the simmered 'nibuta' style is said to have become the standard at Japanese ramen shops instead.
source_title: チャーシューと焼き豚の違いは"調理法"にあった｜煮豚・叉焼の境界線まで徹底解説

name_en: Happosai — a stir-fry of pork and mixed vegetables in a thick soy-chicken sauce
summary_ja: 豚肉や白菜、うずらの卵など多くの具材を炒め合わせ、とろみをつけた餡に仕立てる料理。中国では「八」が実際に八種類の具材を指すが、日本では「五目」と同じく具材の数にこだわらない言葉として広まったとされる。
summary_en: Pork, napa cabbage, quail egg, and more are stir-fried together into a thick sauce — in China 'eight' is said to mean literally eight ingredients, but in Japan the word spread more loosely, closer to 'gomoku,' with no fixed ingredient count.
